writer.source: CLDR RBNF fr_CH (common/rbnf as shipped in unicode-rbnf 2.5.1). French counts in the long scale: "milliard" for 10^9 and "billion" for 10^12. Académie française, «Questions de langue: nombres»: the traditional spelling joins with a hyphen the numerals below one hundred and links the others with a space; "il est également possible, en accord avec les Rectifications de l'orthographe ... de lier par un trait d'union tous les éléments qui composent le nombre". The writer prints the traditional spelling; the reader reads both

fraction.source: Académie française, «Questions de langue: nombres» is not quoted for fractions. Not checked: the numerator is a cardinal and the denominator a plural ordinal, with "demi", "tiers" and "quart" for 2, 3 and 4; "tiers" is the same in the plural.
